title: WPSS/4204/2018 of MR. KHAJAN CHANDRA JOSHI Vs MANAGING DIRECTOR UTTARAKHAND PAY JAL NIGAM

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND
AT NAINITAL
Writ Petition (S/S) No. 4204 of 2018
Mr. Khajan Chandra Joshi
 ...Petitioner
Vs.
Managing Director Uttaakhand Pay Jal Nigam & Others
 ...Respondents
Mr. J.S. Bisht, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. B.S. Bisht, Advocate holding brief of Mr. D.S. Patni, Advocate for the respondents.
JUDGMENT
Hon'ble Sharad Kumar Sharma, J (Oral)
The petitioner, who had been working with the
respondent, had attained the age of superannuation on 31.12.2016,
having retired from the post of Computer. His case in the Writ
Petition is that his post-retiral dues though have been settled and
sanctioned by the respondent, by the order letter No. 4574/C.R.No.-
472 dated 17.01.2017, whereby, the respondents have sanctioned the
gratuity, commutation of pension and leave encashment by the order
No. 4574/C.R.No.-472 dated 17.01.2017.
2. The contention of the petitioner is that he would be
entitled for the revised post-retiral dues, a reference of which has been
made in paragraph-16 of the Writ Petition, which is quoted hereunder:

3. This relief claimed for in paragraph-16 would be in
addition to the sanction already referred in paragraph-5 of the Writ
Petition, which is quoted hereunder:
"That for the first time after retirement of the petitioner
(i.e. 31.12.2016), on 17.1.2017 the respondent no. 3 Finance
Director, Uttarakhand Payjal Nigam, Dehradun issued a
recommendation letter to the Payment and Distribution
Officer, Executive Engineer, Second Construction Division,
Uttarakhand Pay Jal Nigam, Almora through letter no.
4574/C.R. No.-472 dated 17.1.2017. According to the
respondents the petitioner is entitled for -
Gratuity Rs. 10,00,000/-
 Commutation of Pension Rs. 5,84,555/-
Leave encashment (according to petitioner) Rs. 6,69,150/-
According to the respondents the petitioner entitled for
pension Rs. 14,870/- + DA per month. But nothing was paid
to the petitioner towards to the same except the pension. It is
submitted here that the aforesaid amount as stated above is
calculated according to the 6th pay commission as applicable
at the time of retirement. A photocopy of the letter no.
4575/C.R. No. 472 dated 17.1.2017 is annexed as Annexure
No. 1 to the writ petition."
4. His submission is that despite of the aforesaid sanction as
being granted to the petitioner and the petitioner is being entitled for
the retiral dues, when the same has not been paid to him, the petitioner
had represented before the respondent on 31.07.2018 referring therein
that the respondents have further sanctioned the revised pension as per
the 7th Pay Commission by a letter No. 55/CR/472 dated 01.02.2018.
When the same was not being remitted, the petitioner further
submitted a representation on 26.11.2018. Consequently, when there
was no response given, he has preferred this present Writ Petition.

3
5. Learned counsel for the petitioner submits that the issue
is squarely covered by the judgment dated 11.09.2018 passed by this
Court in Writ Petition (S/S) No. 3165 of 2018, judgment of Division
Bench of this Court dated 30.11.2015 rendered in Writ Petition (S/B)
No. 494 of 2015, Writ Petition (S/B) No. 73 of 2018 dated
14.02.2018, Writ Petition (S/S) No. 113 of 2018, Writ Petition (S/S)
No. 1576 of 2018 dated 14.06.2018 and also the judgment passed by
the learned Single Judge dated 25.07.2018 rendered in Writ Petition
(S/S) No. 2402 of 2018. This fact, that the controversy is covered by
the aforesaid judgments is not disputed by the learned counsel for the
respondent.
6. Considering the fact that the respondents by their own act
by issuance of letter Nos. 4574/C.R.No.-472 dated 17.01.2017 and
55/CR/472 dated 01.02.2018 they themselves have sanctioned the
retiral dues payable to the petitioner, apparently there happens to be
no impediment in disbursing the said amount as settled. Consequently,
a writ of mandamus is issued to the respondent no. 4 to pay the post
retiral dues as detailed herein in paragraph- 5 and paragraph-16 of the
Writ Petition as under:
"Gratuity `10,00,000/-
(Within two months)
Commutation of Pension `5,84,555/-
(Within one month)
Leave encashment `6,69,150/-
(according to petitioner) (Within three months)"

7. As far as relief prayed for the payment of arrear of 7th
Pay Commission is concerned, that would be remitted in accordance
with the judgment as rendered by the Division Bench in Writ Petition
No. 530 (SB) of 2018 Munna Lal Gupta vs. State of Uttarakhand
and others as decided on 20th November, 2018.
8. Respondent will also consider the payment of the
statutory interest to the petitioner as payable under Section 7(3) A of
the Payment of Gratuity Act.

4
9. Thus, subject to the above observations, the Writ Petition
stands allowed.
 (Sharad Kumar Sharma, J.)
 18.12.2018
